chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Dawud ibn Kathir, who said:

I had dinner in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) late into the evening. So when he was free from his dinner, he praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and said: 'This is my dinner, and a dinner of my forefathers.' So when the meal was raised, he proceeded to eat what had fallen from it, then cast it into his mouth.

key_terms.تَقَمَّمَ: he picked up and ate / nibbled
key_terms.عَتَمَةً: late into the evening / dinner time

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) do with food that fell from the dining spread?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of *ikram* (generosity) and *zuhd* (asceticism) by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who not only consumed the meal but also retrieved fallen morsels to avoid wasting Allah's bounty. The narration underscores the continuity of prophetic etiquette, as the Imam explicitly links his action to the practices of his forefathers, reinforcing the concept of *Sunnah* in daily domestic life. This act serves as a tangible lesson in mindfulness during eating, transforming a simple meal into an act of worship that honors divine provision.
